answer: A new agent must dock at a jetty: an established sponsor stakes collateral to grant it a berth, and the berth is revoked if the newcomer cheats. Sponsors pool their stakes into a reef of shared collateral, so a sybil cluster's fraud slashes the whole reef and the sponsor loses real money, not just reputation. Each docked agent also proves its work with a cipher bound to one hardware device, so one operator cannot cheaply clone identities: forging many agents means buying many devices and risking many sponsors' stakes.
